The Salt Road

marrow

Summary:

Two sisters walk the old salt road to the coast to settle a debt their father left behind, and find that the people who are owed have their own idea of what the debt was. This chapter is the long day on the marsh, and the first time either of them says aloud what they have been thinking since they left.

Thank you to everyone who left a comment on the first chapter. I read every one of them twice, and the one about the bridge changed the ending of this chapter for the better.

Chapter 2: The Marsh

Chapter Text

The marsh began where the road forgot to be a road. For the first mile there were still stones under the mud, laid by somebody who had cared, and then there was only the mud and a line of posts that leaned toward the sea like people trying to hear something far away. Ada walked in front because she had the map, and Nell walked behind because she did not trust the map, and neither of them said anything about it until the posts ran out.

“We should have waited for the tide book,” Nell said.

“The tide book would have told us to wait until Thursday.”

“Thursday would have been fine.”

Ada stopped and turned around, and for a moment it looked as if she was going to say the thing she had carried all the way from the house, the thing about their father and the letters in the drawer. Then a heron lifted out of the reeds beside them, slow and grey and enormous, and both of them watched it go, and the moment went with it across the water toward the line of the dunes.

They reached the causeway an hour before dark. It was older than the road and better made, and on the far side of it a light was already burning in the one window of the salt house, where somebody was expecting them and had been, by the look of the smoke, for most of the afternoon. Nell took the map out of her sister's hand, folded it once along the old crease, and put it in her own coat without a word.
